# PR Discussion History _Previous review discussions for PR #675._ ## Review Threads (Inline Comments) ### Thread 1 — `js/factoryState.js` **ai-teammate** (2026-10-03): 🚨 **BLOCKING: merged cards' state history destroys itself within ~4h of the merge** `nextHistory`'s `terminalAt` path appends unconditionally, but merged cards are **rebuilt every tick** while they sit in the 24h `merged_recent` window (`buildFactoryState` re-derives the card from `prevCard` each tick, `js/factoryState.js:493`). So every tick appends *another* `{merged_recent, at: mergedAt}` entry: ```js if (terminalAt) { h.push({ state: key, at: terminalAt }); // no dedupe — pushes every tick return capHistory(h); } ``` Reproduced by chaining `buildFactoryState` over 31 ticks (10-min cadence): ``` tick 1 history: [pr_created, validating, merged_recent@09:30] ← correct after 31 ticks: 24 × {merged_recent, at 09:30} ← real history fully evicted ``` After `HISTORY_CAP` (24) ticks (~4h at the standard 10-min cadence) the card's entire real pipeline timeline (`pr_created → review → approved_queue → validating`) is sliced out of the snapshot. The drawer then renders 24 identical "Merged" rows with `0m` durations — the ticket's headline deliverable (per-state timings for bottleneck analysis) is gone exactly for the cards where it matters most. The new test only covers the *first* merge transition, so it can't see this. **Fix** (one guard — skip the append when the carried history already ends in that state): ```js if (terminalAt) { if (!h.length || h[h.length - 1].state !== key) { h.push({ state: key, at: terminalAt }); } return capHistory(h); } ``` and add a regression test that builds the merged state tick-over-tick and asserts the history length stays at 3 with no duplicate terminal entries. --- ### Thread 2 — `.dmtools/credential-helper.log` **ai-teammate** (2026-10-03): 🚨 **BLOCKING: this PR commits the credential-helper log it claims to gitignore** The diff **adds** `.dmtools/credential-helper.log` as a new tracked file (4 lines of `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN credential served …` trace events) *and* adds the path to `.gitignore`. Those two changes contradict each other: `.gitignore` has **no effect on tracked files**, so the local run artifact is now permanently in the repo and every future run appends more lines that will show up in diffs (this very branch already went through an unresolved both-added merge conflict over this file). Context per `AGENTS.md`: this is a **public, product-agnostic** repo and local dmtools run artifacts must never be committed. The log content contains no secret values (env var *name* + timestamps only), but committing credential-serving traces is exactly the artifact class that must stay out; the PR description itself says the goal was to stop tracking "a previous run accidentally committed it" — the change does the opposite. **Fix:** ```bash git rm --cached .dmtools/credential-helper.log ``` Keep the `.gitignore` line (correct), drop the file from the commit. Please also verify no earlier commit on this branch left the file in history (`git log --all --oneline -- .dmtools/credential-helper.log`) — a history that ever contained it cannot be cleaned by `.gitignore` alone. --- ### Thread 3 — `site/factory/app.js` **ai-teammate** (2026-10-03): ⚠️ **IMPORTANT: development-lane issue cards never open the details drawer** The render pass indexes only PR cards from the pipeline lanes: ```js list.forEach(function (c) { if (c && c.pr != null) boardIndex['pr-' + c.pr + '@' + l.id] = { item: c, repo: st_repo, laneId: l.id }; }); ``` A card in the **development lane** is an issue card, so it gets `data-key="issue-402@development"` — a key that is never added to `boardIndex` (only the backlog columns are indexed below). `onCardClick` → `drawerCtxFor` returns `null` → `preventDefault` is skipped → the click falls through and **navigates to GitHub** instead of opening the drawer. Meanwhile the same issue's backlog twin (`issue-402@in_dev`) opens the drawer fine. Two twins, two different behaviors — and the "In dev" card, the one an operator watches most, is the one that silently loses the feature. Ticket AC says "details drawer works for PRs and issues"; for in-dev issues it only half-works. **Fix:** index issue cards in the lanes loop too (`boardIndex['issue-' + c.issue + '@' + l.id] = …`), or resolve `issue-N@development` to the backlog twin's context in `drawerCtxFor`. --- ### Thread 4 — `site/factory/app.js` **ai-teammate** (2026-10-03): ⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `?fixture=` fetches an arbitrary URL, and snapshot hrefs are not scheme-checked — together they make the board injectable** Two related gaps in the new v3 surfaces: 1. `FIXTURE` comes straight from the query string and is passed to `fetch` unvalidated. Anyone can craft `index.html?fixture=https://attacker.example/payload.json` and render fully attacker-controlled board content (fake PRs, titles, statuses) under this site's origin — a credible spoofing vector for a public board, since the page never indicates the data didn't come from a `factory-data` snapshot. 2. Card/pill hrefs use snapshot fields verbatim (only HTML-escaped): ```js var href = isIssue ? (c.url || CFG.prUrl(c.repo, num, 'issues')) : CFG.prUrl(c.repo, num); ``` `esc()` escapes quotes/angle brackets but **not** URL schemes, so a `"url": "javascript:…"` value in a snapshot (or in a fixture JSON) survives into `href` and executes on click. The live data source is the machine's own factory-data branch (trusted), which is why this is IMPORTANT rather than BLOCKING — but the `?fixture=` param hands the untrusted case to anyone who can paste a link. **Suggested hardening (a few lines total):** - Restrict the fixture to same-origin/relative paths: `if (FIXTURE && /^(https?:)?\/\//.test(FIXTURE) && FIXTURE.indexOf(location.origin) !== 0) FIXTURE = null;` — the visual-check usage (`?fixture=visual-check/fixture.json`) is relative and keeps working. - Allowlist the scheme when building hrefs: `function safeHref(u) { return /^https?:\/\//i.test(u) ? u : ''; }` and fall back to `CFG.prUrl(...)` when the snapshot URL fails the check (also covers `c.repo` shape). --- ### Thread 5 — `js/smAgent.js` **ai-teammate** (2026-10-03): 💡 **SUGGESTION: the backlog silently truncates at the search API's first page and is unbounded** The v3 query fetches ALL open issues (`repo:X is:issue is:open`) in one call. GitHub search returns at most one page per call (30 by default, 100 with `per_page`), and `github_search_issues` here passes no paging — so on a repo with more open issues than one page, the `inbox` bucket (everything unassigned/unlabeled) is **silently truncated** while `backlogCounts` presents the partial view as authoritative ("N total"). Snapshots also grow without a bound as the issue count grows — they're re-published to the data branch every 10 minutes and rendered in full. Practical impact today is low (the active repos have modest open-issue counts), but the snapshot's contract should be honest about completeness. Options: - pass an explicit `perPage`/sort (e.g. `sort:created&order:desc`, newest N) and document the cap next to `backlogCounts`; - or cap the inbox bucket in `buildFactoryState` (e.g. 50 newest) so the JSON size stays bounded regardless of repo; - at minimum, note the page limit in the README's backlog section so a truncated lane isn't mistaken for "empty". The change from the label-filtered query to all-issues is also a behavior change worth a line in the PR description's verify notes: on busy repos the search now matches far more items per tick (cost is fine — still one call — but the payload is not). --- ### Thread 6 — `site/factory/app.js` **ai-teammate** (2026-10-03): 💡 **SUGGESTION: progress-bar aria-label is vacuous** ```js return '
' + ... ``` This always renders `"N of N"` — the one quantity that carries no information (it's the same number twice). For a `role="img"` element the label is what a screen reader gets instead of the bar; make it state the actual progress, e.g.: ```js 'aria-label="' + s.total + ' items: ' + s.done + ' done, ' + s.inflight + ' in flight, ' + s.queued + ' queued' + (s.blocked ? ', ' + s.blocked + ' blocked' : '') + '"' ``` Trivial change, matches the "readable at a glance" goal of the ticket (readable by everyone, including AT users). --- ### Thread 7 — `site/factory/app.js` **ai-teammate** (2026-10-03): 💡 **SUGGESTION: backlog cards render no age, even though the data is right there** `cardHtml` derives the age chip from `LANE_ENTERED_AT[laneId]`, which only has keys for the six pipeline lanes. For backlog columns (`in_dev`/`queued`/`blocked`/inbox`) the lookup is `undefined` → no age chip ever renders on issue cards — yet the snapshot *does* carry the per-card time: `devStartedAt` for in-dev cards and the last `history` entry's `at` (stamped on every bucket transition) for the rest. Extract once near `cardHtml`: ```js function badgesHtml(c) { var hot = CFG.badgeLabels || []; return (c.labels || []).map(function (l) { return '' + esc(l) + ''; }).join(''); } ``` and use it in both places (the href-building block is similarly near-duplicated and could share a small helper, but the badges are the clear win). --- ### Thread 9 — `site/factory/app.js` **ai-teammate** (2026-10-03): 💡 **SUGGESTION: status pill reports "issues: 0 …" for pre-v3 snapshots** `st.backlogCounts` is undefined on snapshots published before this change, so `bc[c.id] || 0` zeroes every bucket and the pill always renders `issues: 0 in-dev · 0 queued · 0 blocked · 0 inbox` — a false "backlog is empty" signal during any window where an old-SM snapshot is still live on a `factory-data` branch (upgrade skew), and today on schema-1 history files. Cheap fix — only claim what the snapshot declares: ```js if (st.backlog) { document.getElementById('backlog-pill').textContent = 'issues: ' + backlogSummary; } else { document.getElementById('backlog-pill').hidden = true; // pre-v3 snapshot } ``` (remember to un-hide it on the next render). Same spirit as the drawer's `"—"` fallback: absent data renders as absent, not as zeros. --- ### Thread 10 — `js/factoryState.js` **ai-teammate** (2026-10-03): 💡 **SUGGESTION: the hardcoded `DEFAULT_MACHINE_AUTHOR` overrides "unconfigured", not just "unset"** ```js var machineAuthor = input.machineAuthor || DEFAULT_MACHINE_AUTHOR; ``` `resolveMachineAuthor` (js/common/machineAuthor.js) deliberately returns **null** when a deployment has configured no `machineAuthor` — that's a meaningful "unconfigured" state, and this `||` collapses it into the hardcoded `'ai-teammate'` login. Safer contract: treat null as "no assignment bucketing" and keep the constant only for tests/back-compat: ```js var machineAuthor = input.machineAuthor || null; ... var assigned = !!machineAuthor && (/* assignees/assignee checks */); ``` Low practical risk (the login is machine-flavored), but it's the kind of silent default that surprises the next factory adopting the board. --- ### Thread 11 **ai-teammate** (2026-10-03): ## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES **Summary**: Two blocking issues: (1) merged cards' state history self-corrupts — the `terminalAt` path in `nextHistory` appends a duplicate `merged_recent` entry on every tick, and after `HISTORY_CAP` (24) ticks (~4h at the 10-min cadence) the card's real pipeline timeline is evicted, defeating the drawer's timings feature exactly for merged cards (verified with a repro); (2) the PR commits `.dmtools/credential-helper.log` as a tracked file while adding it to `.gitignore` — gitignore can't untrack a file, so the local artifact stays in this public, product-agnostic repo. Dedupe the terminal history append (skip when the last carried entry is already that state) + add a tick-over-tick regression test 2. `git rm --cached .dmtools/credential-helper.log` and verify the file never landed in branch history 3. Ticket AC says "details drawer works for PRs and issues"; for in-dev issues it only half-works. **Fix:** index issue cards in the lanes loop too (`boardIndex['issue-' + c.issue + '@' + l.id] = …`), or resolve `issue-N@development` to the backlog twin's context in `drawerCtxFor`. --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-03): ⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `?fixture=` fetches an arbitrary URL, and snapshot hrefs are not scheme-checked — together they make the board injectable** Two related gaps in the new v3 surfaces: 1. `FIXTURE` comes straight from the query string and is passed to `fetch` unvalidated. Anyone can craft `index.html?fixture=https://attacker.example/payload.json` and render fully attacker-controlled board content (fake PRs, titles, statuses) under this site's origin — a credible spoofing vector for a public board, since the page never indicates the data didn't come from a `factory-data` snapshot. 2. Card/pill hrefs use snapshot fields verbatim (only HTML-escaped): ```js var href = isIssue ? (c.url || CFG.prUrl(c.repo, num, 'issues')) : CFG.prUrl(c.repo, num); ``` `esc()` escapes quotes/angle brackets but **not** URL schemes, so a `"url": "javascript:…"` value in a snapshot (or in a fixture JSON) survives into `href` and executes on click. The live data source is the machine's own factory-data branch (trusted), which is why this is IMPORTANT rather than BLOCKING — but the `?fixture=` param hands the untrusted case to anyone who can paste a link. **Suggested hardening (a few lines total):** - Restrict the fixture to same-origin/relative paths: `if (FIXTURE && /^(https?:)?\/\//.test(FIXTURE) && FIXTURE.indexOf(location.origin) !== 0) FIXTURE = null;` — the visual-check usage (`?fixture=visual-check/fixture.json`) is relative and keeps working. - Allowlist the scheme when building hrefs: `function safeHref(u) { return /^https?:\/\//i.test(u) ? u : ''; }` and fall back to `CFG.prUrl(...)` when the snapshot URL fails the check (also covers `c.repo` shape). --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-03): 💡 **SUGGESTION: the backlog silently truncates at the search API's first page and is unbounded** The v3 query fetches ALL open issues (`repo:X is:issue is:open`) in one call. GitHub search returns at most one page per call (30 by default, 100 with `per_page`), and `github_search_issues` here passes no paging — so on a repo with more open issues than one page, the `inbox` bucket (everything unassigned/unlabeled) is **silently truncated** while `backlogCounts` presents the partial view as authoritative ("N total"). Snapshots also grow without a bound as the issue count grows — they're re-published to the data branch every 10 minutes and rendered in full. Practical impact today is low (the active repos have modest open-issue counts), but the snapshot's contract should be honest about completeness. Options: - pass an explicit `perPage`/sort (e.g. `sort:created&order:desc`, newest N) and document the cap next to `backlogCounts`; - or cap the inbox bucket in `buildFactoryState` (e.g. 50 newest) so the JSON size stays bounded regardless of repo; - at minimum, note the page limit in the README's backlog section so a truncated lane isn't mistaken for "empty". The change from the label-filtered query to all-issues is also a behavior change worth a line in the PR description's verify notes: on busy repos the search now matches far more items per tick (cost is fine — still one call — but the payload is not). --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-03): 💡 **SUGGESTION: progress-bar aria-label is vacuous** ```js return '
' + ... ``` This always renders `"N of N"` — the one quantity that carries no information (it's the same number twice). For a `role="img"` element the label is what a screen reader gets instead of the bar; make it state the actual progress, e.g.: ```js 'aria-label="' + s.total + ' items: ' + s.done + ' done, ' + s.inflight + ' in flight, ' + s.queued + ' queued' + (s.blocked ? ', ' + s.blocked + ' blocked' : '') + '"' ``` Trivial change, matches the "readable at a glance" goal of the ticket (readable by everyone, including AT users). --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-03): 💡 **SUGGESTION: backlog cards render no age, even though the data is right there** `cardHtml` derives the age chip from `LANE_ENTERED_AT[laneId]`, which only has keys for the six pipeline lanes. For backlog columns (`in_dev`/`queued`/`blocked`/inbox`) the lookup is `undefined` → no age chip ever renders on issue cards — yet the snapshot *does* carry the per-card time: `devStartedAt` for in-dev cards and the last `history` entry's `at` (stamped on every bucket transition) for the rest. Suggested: when `LANE_ENTERED_AT[laneId]` misses, fall back to the newest history entry: ```js var enteredAt = c[LANE_ENTERED_AT[laneId]]; if (!enteredAt && c.history && c.history.length) { var last = c.history[c.history.length - 1]; enteredAt = last.at || null; // first-ever entry may have no `at` — honest unknown } ``` That gives every backlog card a "how long has it been sitting here" chip — arguably the most useful number in the new lanes (age of the inbox, age of the block). --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-03): 💡 **SUGGESTION: badge HTML is duplicated between `cardHtml` and `drawerHeaderHtml`** These two blocks are byte-identical (hot-label highlighting + the `blocked` class): ```js var badges = (c.labels || []).map(function (l) { return '' + esc(l) + ''; }).join(''); ``` The card and the drawer must stay visually consistent by construction, not by copy-paste — the next label-styling tweak (e.g. adding `agent:dev` coloring) will land in one and miss the other. Extract once near `cardHtml`: ```js function badgesHtml(c) { var hot = CFG.badgeLabels || []; return (c.labels || []).map(function (l) { return '' + esc(l) + ''; }).join(''); } ``` and use it in both places (the href-building block is similarly near-duplicated and could share a small helper, but the badges are the clear win). --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-03): 💡 **SUGGESTION: status pill reports "issues: 0 …" for pre-v3 snapshots** `st.backlogCounts` is undefined on snapshots published before this change, so `bc[c.id] || 0` zeroes every bucket and the pill always renders `issues: 0 in-dev · 0 queued · 0 blocked · 0 inbox` — a false "backlog is empty" signal during any window where an old-SM snapshot is still live on a `factory-data` branch (upgrade skew), and today on schema-1 history files. Cheap fix — only claim what the snapshot declares: ```js if (st.backlog) { document.getElementById('backlog-pill').textContent = 'issues: ' + backlogSummary; } else { document.getElementById('backlog-pill').hidden = true; // pre-v3 snapshot } ``` (remember to un-hide it on the next render). Same spirit as the drawer's `"—"` fallback: absent data renders as absent, not as zeros. --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-03): 💡 **SUGGESTION: the hardcoded `DEFAULT_MACHINE_AUTHOR` overrides "unconfigured", not just "unset"** ```js var machineAuthor = input.machineAuthor || DEFAULT_MACHINE_AUTHOR; ``` `resolveMachineAuthor` (js/common/machineAuthor.js) deliberately returns **null** when a deployment has configured no `machineAuthor` — that's a meaningful "unconfigured" state, and this `||` collapses it into the hardcoded `'ai-teammate'` login. For a factory that never set the knob, any issue assigned to a user literally named `ai-teammate` (or to whatever that fallback string matches in their org) would land in the "In dev · assigned" lane without the deployment ever opting in. The header comment calls it a "deployment knob" — a knob should have no opinion when unset. Safer contract: treat null as "no assignment bucketing" and keep the constant only for tests/back-compat: ```js var machineAuthor = input.machineAuthor || null; ... var assigned = !!machineAuthor && (/* assignees/assignee checks */); ``` Low practical risk (the login is machine-flavored), but it's the kind of silent default that surprises the next factory adopting the board. --- **ai-teammate** (2026-10-03): ## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES **Summary**: Two blocking issues: (1) merged cards' state history self-corrupts — the `terminalAt` path in `nextHistory` appends a duplicate `merged_recent` entry on every tick, and after `HISTORY_CAP` (24) ticks (~4h at the 10-min cadence) the card's real pipeline timeline is evicted, defeating the drawer's timings feature exactly for merged cards (verified with a repro); (2) the PR commits `.dmtools/credential-helper.log` as a tracked file while adding it to `.gitignore` — gitignore can't untrack a file, so the local artifact stays in this public, product-agnostic repo. Two important findings: development-lane issue cards never open the details drawer (only PR cards are indexed in `boardIndex`, so in-dev issues — a ticket AC — navigate away instead), and `?fixture=` fetches an arbitrary URL while snapshot hrefs skip scheme checks (`javascript:` survives `esc()`). Tests verified: +21 passing (1251→1272) with an identical 45-failure baseline on `main`; Pages deploy exclusion for `visual-check` pre-exists and holds. **Key Issues**: - 🚨 `js/factoryState.js:156` — duplicate terminal history entries flush real merged-card timelines within ~4h - 🚨 `.dmtools/credential-helper.log` — tracked artifact contradicting the PR's own `.gitignore` intent; `git rm --cached` needed - ⚠️ `site/factory/app.js:540` — dev-lane issue cards fall through to GitHub nav instead of opening the drawer - ⚠️ `site/factory/app.js:572` — `?fixture=` arbitrary-URL fetch + unvalidated href schemes (content injection / `javascript:` href) - 💡 6 suggestions: backlog first-page truncation + unbounded snapshot, vacuous progress-bar aria-label, no age chip on backlog cards, duplicated badge HTML, misleading "issues: 0" pill on pre-v3 snapshots, `DEFAULT_MACHINE_AUTHOR` overriding "unconfigured" **Next Steps**: 1. Dedupe the terminal history append (skip when the last carried entry is already that state) + add a tick-over-tick regression test 2. `git rm --cached .dmtools/credential-helper.log` and verify the file never landed in branch history 3. Index issue cards in the lanes loop (or alias to the backlog twin) so the drawer opens from the dev lane 4. Restrict `?fixture=` to same-origin and allowlist `http(s)` hrefs 5. Remaining suggestions are non-blocking polish — address in this PR or follow up ---

  "fields": {
    "summary": "Factory Board v3 — readable progress, details drawer (state history + timings), issue backlog lanes, token spend",
    "description": "# Factory Board v3 — readable progress, details drawer, backlog lanes, token spend

Owner-directed (2026-10-03). The board at `site/factory/` (zero-build, state snapshots from `factory-data` branches) needs four upgrades. All data must keep coming from the SM tick snapshots — no new scrapers.

## 1. Progress line is unreadable

Dots now encode per-PR status, but it's impossible to answer "how much is left" at a glance. Replace/augment the dot row per lane with a compact summary: `N total · M done · K in-flight · Q queued` (+ blocked count where relevant) and a thin progress bar per lane. Dots may stay as decoration, the numbers must be readable.

## 2. Click → details drawer → PR

Clicking a PR (dot, card, or row) opens a details drawer (inline panel, no page nav):
- header: PR number, title, head sha, current state + labels, **link to the PR** (opens github.com in a new tab)
- body: **full state history** — the sequence of states this PR went through with timestamps (from the snapshot history), newest first
- **timings** — how long the PR sat in each state (`validating 42m`, `approved→validated 5m`, `parked 2h13m`), so bottlenecks are analyzable later. Raw durations + a simple bar per state.

## 3. Issues as backlog lanes

The board shows PRs only; issues are invisible. Add a backlog section fed by the same snapshots (extend the SM tick snapshot with open issues: number, title, assignee, labels):
- columns by state: **assigned to ai-teammate (in dev)** · **agent:dev queued** · **blocked** (the `blocked` label = owner hold, must be its own column and visually distinct) · inbox (no label/assignee)
- each issue clickable → same details drawer (issue states: assigned → dev → PR opened → …), link to the issue.

## 4. Token spend per action (details)

fa legs already report token usage (bench); more factories will follow. Extend the snapshot with per-leg token counters (prompt/completion/total per run where available) and show them in the details drawer: per-action table (leg, when, tokens) + a per-PR total. Graceful "—" when a factory doesn't report tokens yet — schema stays optional.

## Acceptance

- Board still zero-build, still reads `factory-data` snapshots (schema addition = additive, old snapshots keep rendering).
- Lane summaries readable at a glance; details drawer works for PRs and issues; timings render; token table renders with fallback.
- `visual-check` fixtures updated for the new surfaces (see `site/factory/visual-check/`).
- Pages deploy stays green.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 675
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/675
- **Title**: gh-672 Factory Board v3 — readable progress, details drawer (state history + timings), issue backlog lanes, token spend
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-672` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1449
- **Deletions**: -74
- **Created**: 2026-10-03T20:05:50Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-03T21:09:39Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Factory Board v3 (`site/factory/`) + additive snapshot schema v3 (`js/factoryState.js`, `js/smAgent.js`): readable per-lane progress, a click-to-open details drawer, issue backlog lanes, and optional per-leg token spend — all fed by the same SM tick snapshots, no new scrapers.

### Key decisions
- **Schema stays 2, all additions optional**: per-card `history` (state timeline, accumulated tick-over-tick like the v2 timestamps, capped at 24), top-level `backlog` (buckets: `blocked` label > assigned to `machineAuthor` > `agent:dev` > inbox), optional per-card `tokens` (leg/at/prompt/completion/total). Old snapshots keep rendering; the drawer derives a timeline from v2 timestamp fields when `history` is absent and renders `tokens — not reported by this factory` as fallback.
- **Token source is a contract, not a scraper**: factories whose legs report usage (fa's bench) drop a keyed JSON file (`statePublish.tokensFile`, default `outputs/token_usage/factory_tokens.json`); `readTokensFile()` degrades to null on any miss — never fails the tick.
- **One search call per tick** now fetches ALL open issues (`repo:X is:issue is:open`), feeding both the development lane and the backlog; dev-lane and backlog twins of an issue share one history array.
- **Board**: cards keep their GitHub href (middle-click/new tab) but a plain click opens the inline drawer (state history newest-first, `2h13m`-style per-state timings with proportional bars, token table with per-card total; esc/backdrop/✕ close). # PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #675._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/factoryState.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-03):
🚨 **BLOCKING: merged cards' state history destroys itself within ~4h of the merge**

`nextHistory`'s `terminalAt` path appends unconditionally, but merged cards are **rebuilt every tick** while they sit in the 24h `merged_recent` window (`buildFactoryState` re-derives the card from `prevCard` each tick, `js/factoryState.js:493`). So every tick appends *another* `{merged_recent, at: mergedAt}` entry:

```js
if (terminalAt) {
    h.push({ state: key, at: terminalAt });   // no dedupe — pushes every tick
    return capHistory(h);
}
```

Reproduced by chaining `buildFactoryState` over 31 ticks (10-min cadence):

```
tick 1 history: [pr_created, validating, merged_recent@09:30]   ← correct
after 31 ticks: 24 × {merged_recent, at 09:30}                  ← real history fully evicted
```

After `HISTORY_CAP` (24) ticks (~4h at the standard 10-min cadence) the card's entire real pipeline timeline (`pr_created → review → approved_queue → validating`) is sliced out of the snapshot. The drawer then renders 24 identical "Merged" rows with `0m` durations — the ticket's headline deliverable (per-state timings for bottleneck analysis) is gone exactly for the cards where it matters most. The new test only covers the *first* merge transition, so it can't see this.

**Fix** (one guard — skip the append when the carried history already ends in that state):

```js
if (terminalAt) {
    if (!h.length || h[h.length - 1].state !== key) {
        h.push({ state: key, at: terminalAt });
    }
    return capHistory(h);
}
```

and add a regression test that builds the merged state tick-over-tick and asserts the history length stays at 3 with no duplicate terminal entries.

---

### Thread 2 — `.dmtools/credential-helper.log`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-03):
🚨 **BLOCKING: this PR commits the credential-helper log it claims to gitignore**

The diff **adds** `.dmtools/credential-helper.log` as a new tracked file (4 lines of `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN credential served …` trace events) *and* adds the path to `.gitignore`. Those two changes contradict each other: `.gitignore` has **no effect on tracked files**, so the local run artifact is now permanently in the repo and every future run appends more lines that will show up in diffs (this very branch already went through an unresolved both-added merge conflict over this file).

Context per `AGENTS.md`: this is a **public, product-agnostic** repo and local dmtools run artifacts must never be committed. The log content contains no secret values (env var *name* + timestamps only), but committing credential-serving traces is exactly the artifact class that must stay out; the PR description itself says the goal was to stop tracking "a previous run accidentally committed it" — the change does the opposite.

**Fix:**

```bash
git rm --cached .dmtools/credential-helper.log
```

Keep the `.gitignore` line (correct), drop the file from the commit. Please also verify no earlier commit on this branch left the file in history (`git log --all --oneline -- .dmtools/credential-helper.log`) — a history that ever contained it cannot be cleaned by `.gitignore` alone.

---

### Thread 3 — `site/factory/app.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-03):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: development-lane issue cards never open the details drawer**

The render pass indexes only PR cards from the pipeline lanes:

```js
list.forEach(function (c) {
    if (c && c.pr != null) boardIndex['pr-' + c.pr + '@' + l.id] =
      { item: c, repo: st_repo, laneId: l.id };
});
```

A card in the **development lane** is an issue card, so it gets `data-key="issue-402@development"` — a key that is never added to `boardIndex` (only the backlog columns are indexed below). `onCardClick` → `drawerCtxFor` returns `null` → `preventDefault` is skipped → the click falls through and **navigates to GitHub** instead of opening the drawer. Meanwhile the same issue's backlog twin (`issue-402@in_dev`) opens the drawer fine. Two twins, two different behaviors — and the "In dev" card, the one an operator watches most, is the one that silently loses the feature.

Ticket AC says "details drawer works for PRs and issues"; for in-dev issues it only half-works.

**Fix:** index issue cards in the lanes loop too (`boardIndex['issue-' + c.issue + '@' + l.id] = …`), or resolve `issue-N@development` to the backlog twin's context in `drawerCtxFor`.

---

### Thread 4 — `site/factory/app.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-03):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `?fixture=` fetches an arbitrary URL, and snapshot hrefs are not scheme-checked — together they make the board injectable**

Two related gaps in the new v3 surfaces:

1. `FIXTURE` comes straight from the query string and is passed to `fetch` unvalidated. Anyone can craft
   `index.html?fixture=https://attacker.example/payload.json` and render fully attacker-controlled board content (fake PRs, titles, statuses) under this site's origin — a credible spoofing vector for a public board, since the page never indicates the data didn't come from a `factory-data` snapshot.

2. Card/pill hrefs use snapshot fields verbatim (only HTML-escaped):
   ```js
   var href = isIssue ? (c.url || CFG.prUrl(c.repo, num, 'issues')) : CFG.prUrl(c.repo, num);
   ```
   `esc()` escapes quotes/angle brackets but **not** URL schemes, so a `"url": "javascript:…"` value in a snapshot (or in a fixture JSON) survives into `href` and executes on click. The live data source is the machine's own factory-data branch (trusted), which is why this is IMPORTANT rather than BLOCKING — but the `?fixture=` param hands the untrusted case to anyone who can paste a link.

**Suggested hardening (a few lines total):**
- Restrict the fixture to same-origin/relative paths: `if (FIXTURE && /^(https?:)?\/\//.test(FIXTURE) && FIXTURE.indexOf(location.origin) !== 0) FIXTURE = null;` — the visual-check usage (`?fixture=visual-check/fixture.json`) is relative and keeps working.
- Allowlist the scheme when building hrefs: `function safeHref(u) { return /^https?:\/\//i.test(u) ? u : ''; }` and fall back to `CFG.prUrl(...)` when the snapshot URL fails the check (also covers `c.repo` shape).

---

### Thread 5 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-03):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the backlog silently truncates at the search API's first page and is unbounded**

The v3 query fetches ALL open issues (`repo:X is:issue is:open`) in one call. GitHub search returns at most one page per call (30 by default, 100 with `per_page`), and `github_search_issues` here passes no paging — so on a repo with more open issues than one page, the `inbox` bucket (everything unassigned/unlabeled) is **silently truncated** while `backlogCounts` presents the partial view as authoritative ("N total"). Snapshots also grow without a bound as the issue count grows — they're re-published to the data branch every 10 minutes and rendered in full.

Practical impact today is low (the active repos have modest open-issue counts), but the snapshot's contract should be honest about completeness. Options:

- pass an explicit `perPage`/sort (e.g. `sort:created&order:desc`, newest N) and document the cap next to `backlogCounts`;
- or cap the inbox bucket in `buildFactoryState` (e.g. 50 newest) so the JSON size stays bounded regardless of repo;
- at minimum, note the page limit in the README's backlog section so a truncated lane isn't mistaken for "empty".

The change from the label-filtered query to all-issues is also a behavior change worth a line in the PR description's verify notes: on busy repos the search now matches far more items per tick (cost is fine — still one call — but the payload is not).

---

### Thread 6 — `site/factory/app.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-03):
💡 **SUGGESTION: progress-bar aria-label is vacuous**

```js
return '<div class="lane-bar" role="img" aria-label="' + s.total + ' of ' +
  s.total + '">' + ...
```

This always renders `"N of N"` — the one quantity that carries no information (it's the same number twice). For a `role="img"` element the label is what a screen reader gets instead of the ba…

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…
Let me start by reading the input context files as instructed.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 675
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/675
- **Title**: gh-672 Factory Board v3 — readable progress, details drawer (state history + timings), issue backlog lanes, token spend
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-672` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1449
- **Deletions**: -74
- **Created**: 2026-10-03T20:05:50Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-03T21:09:39Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Factory Board v3 (`site/factory/`) + additive snapshot schema v3 (`js/factoryState.js`, `js/smAgent.js`): readable per-lane progress, a click-to-open details drawer, issue backlog lanes, and optional per-leg token spend — all fed by the same SM tick snapshots, no new scrapers.

### Key decisions
- **Schema stays 2, all additions optional**: per-card `history` (state timeline, accumulated tick-over-tick like the v2 timestamps, capped at 24), top-level `backlog` (buckets: `blocked` label > assigned to `machineAuthor` > `agent:dev` > inbox), optional per-card `tokens` (leg/at/prompt/completion/total). Old snapshots keep rendering; the drawer derives a timeline from v2 timestamp fields when `history` is absent and renders `tokens — not reported by this factory` as fallback.
- **Token source is a contract, not a scraper**: factories whose legs report usage (fa's bench) drop a keyed JSON file (`statePublish.tokensFile`, default `outputs/token_usage/factory_tokens.json`); `readTokensFile()` degrades to null on any miss — never fails the tick.
- **One search call per tick** now fetches ALL open issues (`repo:X is:issue is:open`), feeding both the development lane and the backlog; dev-lane and backlog twins of an issue share one history array.
- **Board**: cards keep their GitHub href (middle-click/new tab) but a plain click opens the inline drawer (state history newest-first, `2h13m`-style per-state timings with proportional bars, token table with per-card total; esc/backdrop/✕ close). Backlog renders as four columns under the pipeline, blocked visually distinct. `?fixture=` + bundled `visual-check/fixture.json` pin "now" for deterministic captures; `?drawer=pr-817@validating` deep-links.
- Fixed a latent carry bug en route: `prevIndex` resolves an issue to its backlog card, so `devStartedAt` now rides the backlog twin too (regression-tested).
- Added `.dmtools/credential-helper.log` to `.gitignore` (local credential log — a previous run accidentally committed it).

### How to verify
```bash
FILES=$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js $FILES   # 1272 pass; the 45 failures are the known harness mock gaps (baseline 1251/45 — same set)
bash site/factory/visual-check/capture.sh      # regenerates the 5 fixture PNGs (needs headless chromium)
# or open: site/factory/index.html?fixture=visual-check/fixture.json&drawer=pr-817@validating
```
`js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` grew 29→50 tests (history accumulation, backlog bucketing, tokens normalization, tokens-file contract, devStartedAt carry). Visual-check fixtures regenerated for the new surfaces at all four viewports plus a drawer-open frame; pages deploy stays green (fixtures are excluded from `_site`).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SM[SM tick] -->|"gh search: all open issues"| FS[buildFactoryState]
  SM -->|optional tokens file| FS
  FS -->|"lanes + history + backlog + tokens (schema 2, additive)"| PUB[publish → factory-data branch]
  PUB --> BOARD[site/factory board]
  BOARD --> SUM[lane summaries + progress bars]
  BOARD --> BL[backlog: in_dev · queued · blocked · inbox]
  BOARD --> DR[details drawer: history + timings + tokens]
```

</details>

# gh-672: Factory Board v3 — readable progress, details drawer (state history + timings), issue backlog lanes, token spend

## Description

# Factory Board v3 — readable progress, details drawer, backlog lanes, token spend

Owner-directed (2026-10-03). The board at `site/factory/` (zero-build, state snapshots from `factory-data` branches) needs four upgrades. All data must keep coming from the SM tick snapshots — no new scrapers.

## 1. Progress line is unreadable

Dots now encode per-PR status, but it's impossible to answer "how much is left" at a glance. Replace/augment the dot row per lane with a compact summary: `N total · M done · K in-flight · Q queued` (+ blocked count where relevant) and a thin progress bar per lane. Dots may stay as decoration, the numbers must be readable.

## 2. Click → details drawer → PR

Clicking a PR (dot, card, or row) opens a details drawer (inline panel, no page nav):
- header: PR number, title, head sha, current state + labels, **link to the PR** (opens github.com in a new tab)
- body: **full state history** — the sequence of states this PR went through with timestamps (from the snapshot history), newest first
- **timings** — how long the PR sat in each state (`validating 42m`, `approved→validated 5m`, `parked 2h13m`), so bottlenecks are analyzable later. Raw durations + a simple bar per state.

## 3. Issues as backlog lanes

The board shows PRs only; issues are invisible. Add a backlog section fed by the same snapshots (extend the SM tick snapshot with open issues: number, title, assignee, labels):
- columns by state: **assigned to ai-teammate (in dev)** · **agent:dev queued** · **blocked** (the `blocked` label = owner hold, must be its own column and visually distinct) · inbox (no label/assignee)
- each issue clickable → same details drawer (issue states: assigned → dev → PR opened → …), link to the issue.

## 4. Token spend per action (details)

fa legs already report token usage (bench); more factories will follow. Extend the snapshot with per-leg token counters (prompt/completion/total per run where available) and show them in the details drawer: per-action table (leg, when, tokens) + a per-PR total. Graceful "—" when a factory doesn't report tokens yet — schema stays optional.

## Acceptance

- Board still zero-build, still reads `factory-data` snapshots (schema addition = additive, old snapshots keep rendering).
- Lane summaries readable at a glance; details drawer works for PRs and issues; timings render; token table renders with fallback.
- `visual-check` fixtures updated for the new surfaces (see `site/factory/visual-check/`).
- Pages deploy stays green.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #675._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/factoryState.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-03):
🚨 **BLOCKING: merged cards' state history destroys itself within ~4h of the merge**

`nextHistory`'s `terminalAt` path appends unconditionally, but merged cards are **rebuilt every tick** while they sit in the 24h `merged_recent` window (`buildFactoryState` re-derives the card from `prevCard` each tick, `js/factoryState.js:493`). So every tick appends *another* `{merged_recent, at: mergedAt}` entry:

```js
if (terminalAt) {
    h.push({ state: key, at: terminalAt });   // no dedupe — pushes every tick
    return capHistory(h);
}
```

Reproduced by chaining `buildFactoryState` over 31 ticks (10-min cadence):

```
tick 1 history: [pr_created, validating, merged_recent@09:30]   ← correct
after 31 ticks: 24 × {merged_recent, at 09:30}                  ← real history fully evicted
```

After `HISTORY_CAP` (24) ticks (~4h at the standard 10-min cadence) the card's entire real pipeline timeline (`pr_created → review → approved_queue → validating`) is sliced out of the snapshot. The drawer then renders 24 identical "Merged" rows with `0m` durations — the ticket's headline deliverable (per-state timings for bottleneck analysis) is gone exactly for the cards where it matters most. The new test only covers the *first* merge transition, so it can't see this.

**Fix** (one guard — skip the append when the carried history already ends in that state):

```js
if (terminalAt) {
    if (!h.length || h[h.length - 1].state !== key) {
        h.push({ state: key, at: terminalAt });
    }
    return capHistory(h);
}
```

and add a regression test that builds the merged state tick-over-tick and asserts the history length stays at 3 with no duplicate terminal entries.

---

### Thread 2 — `.dmtools/credential-helper.log`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-03):
🚨 **BLOCKING: this PR commits the credential-helper log it claims to gitignore**

The diff **adds** `.dmtools/credential-helper.log` as a new tracked file (4 lines of `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN credential served …` trace events) *and* adds the path to `.gitignore`. Those two changes contradict each other: `.gitignore` has **no effect on tracked files**, so the local run artifact is now permanently in the repo and every future run appends more lines that will show up in diffs (this very branch already went through an unresolved both-added merge conflict over this file).

Context per `AGENTS.md`: this is a **public, product-agnostic** repo and local dmtools run artifacts must never be committed. The log content contains no secret values (env var *name* + timestamps only), but committing credential-serving traces is exactly the artifact class that must stay out; the PR description itself says the goal was to stop tracking "a previous run accidentally committed it" — the change does the opposite.

**Fix:**

```bash
git rm --cached .dmtools/credential-helper.log
```

Keep the `.gitignore` line (correct), drop the file from the commit. Please also verify no earlier commit on this branch left the file in history (`git log --all --oneline -- .dmtools/credential-helper.log`) — a history that ever contained it cannot be cleaned by `.gitignore` alone.

---

### Thread 3 — `site/factory/app.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-03):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: development-lane issue cards never open the details drawer**

The render pass indexes only PR cards from the pipeline lanes:

```js
list.forEach(function (c) {
    if (c && c.pr != null) boardIndex['pr-' + c.pr + '@' + l.id] =
      { item: c, repo: st_repo, laneId: l.id };
});
```

A card in the **development lane** is an issue card, so it gets `data-key="issue-402@development"` — a key that is never added to `boardIndex` (only the backlog columns are indexed below). `onCardClick` → `drawerCtxFor` returns `null` → `preventDefault` is skipped → the click falls through and **navigates to GitHub** instead of opening the drawer. Meanwhile the same issue's backlog twin (`issue-402@in_dev`) opens the drawer fine. Two twins, two different behaviors — and the "In dev" card, the one an operator watches most, is the one that silently loses the feature.

Ticket AC says "details drawer works for PRs and issues"; for in-dev issues it only half-works.

**Fix:** index issue cards in the lanes loop too (`boardIndex['issue-' + c.issue + '@' + l.id] = …`), or resolve `issue-N@development` to the backlog twin's context in `drawerCtxFor`.

---

### Thread 4 — `site/factory/app.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-03):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `?fixture=` fetches an arbitrary URL, and snapshot hrefs are not scheme-checked — together they make the board injectable**

Two related gaps in the new v3 surfaces:

1. `FIXTURE` comes straight from the query string and is passed to `fetch` unvalidated. Anyone can craft
   `index.html?fixture=https://attacker.example/payload.json` and render fully attacker-controlled board content (fake PRs, titles, statuses) under this site's origin — a credible spoofing vector for a public board, since the page never indicates the data didn't come from a `factory-data` snapshot.

2. Card/pill hrefs use snapshot fields verbatim (only HTML-escaped):
   ```js
   var href = isIssue ? (c.url || CFG.prUrl(c.repo, num, 'issues')) : CFG.prUrl(c.repo, num);
   ```
   `esc()` escapes quotes/angle brackets but **not** URL schemes, so a `"url": "javascript:…"` value in a snapshot (or in a fixture JSON) survives into `href` and executes on click. The live data source is the machine's own factory-data branch (trusted), which is why this is IMPORTANT rather than BLOCKING — but the `?fixture=` param hands the untrusted case to anyone who can paste a link.

**Suggested hardening (a few lines total):**
- Restrict the fixture to same-origin/relative paths: `if (FIXTURE && /^(https?:)?\/\//.test(FIXTURE) && FIXTURE.indexOf(location.origin) !== 0) FIXTURE = null;` — the visual-check usage (`?fixture=visual-check/fixture.json`) is relative and keeps working.
- Allowlist the scheme when building hrefs: `function safeHref(u) { return /^https?:\/\//i.test(u) ? u : ''; }` and fall back to `CFG.prUrl(...)` when the snapshot URL fails the check (also covers `c.repo` shape).

---

### Thread 5 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-03):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the backlog silently truncates at the search API's first page and is unbounded**

The v3 query fetches ALL open issues (`repo:X is:issue is:open`) in one call. GitHub search returns at most one page per call (30 by default, 100 with `per_page`), and `github_search_issues` here passes no paging — so on a repo with more open issues than one page, the `inbox` bucket (everything unassigned/unlabeled) is **silently truncated** while `backlogCounts` presents the partial view as authoritative ("N total"). Snapshots also grow without a bound as the issue count grows — they're re-published to the data branch every 10 minutes and rendered in full.

Practical impact today is low (the active repos have modest open-issue counts), but the snapshot's contract should be honest about completeness. Options:

- pass an explicit `perPage`/sort (e.g. `sort:created&order:desc`, newest N) and document the cap next to `backlogCounts`;
- or cap the inbox bucket in `buildFactoryState` (e.g. 50 newest) so the JSON size stays bounded regardless of repo;
- at minimum, note the page limit in the README's backlog section so a truncated lane isn't mistaken for "empty".

The change from the label-filtered query to all-issues is also a behavior change worth a line in the PR description's verify notes: on busy repos the search now matches far more items per tick (cost is fine — still one call — but the payload is not).

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. - **PR #**: 675
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/675
- **Title**: gh-672 Factory Board v3 — readable progress, details drawer (state history + timings), issue backlog lanes, token spend
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-672` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1449
- **Deletions**: -74
- **Created**: 2026-10-03T20:05:50Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-03T21:09:39Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Factory Board v3 (`site/factory/`) + additive snapshot schema v3 (`js/factoryState.js`, `js/smAgent.js`): readable per-lane progress, a click-to-open details drawer, issue backlog lanes, and optional per-leg token spend — all fed by the same SM tick snapshots, no new scrapers.

### Key decisions
- **Schema stays 2, all additions optional**: per-card `history` (state timeline, accumulated tick-over-tick like the v2 timestamps, capped at 24), top-level `backlog` (buckets: `blocked` label > assigned to `machineAuthor` > `agent:dev` > inbox), optional per-card `tokens` (leg/at/prompt/completion/total). Old snapshots keep rendering; the drawer derives a timeline from v2 timestamp fields when `history` is absent and renders `tokens — not reported by this factory` as fallback.
- **Token source is a contract, not a scraper**: factories whose legs report usage (fa's bench) drop a keyed JSON file (`statePublish.tokensFile`, default `outputs/token_usage/factory_tokens.json`); `readTokensFile()` degrades to null on any miss — never fails the tick.
- **One search call per tick** now fetches ALL open issues (`repo:X is:issue is:open`), feeding both the development lane and the backlog; dev-lane and backlog twins of an issue share one history array.
- **Board**: cards keep their GitHub href (middle-click/new tab) but a plain click opens the inline drawer (state history newest-first, `2h13m`-style per-state timings with proportional bars, token table with per-card total; esc/backdrop/✕ close). Backlog renders as four columns under the pipeline, blocked visually distinct. `?fixture=` + bundled `visual-check/fixture.json` pin "now" for deterministic captures; `?drawer=pr-817@validating` deep-links.
- Fixed a latent carry bug en route: `prevIndex` resolves an issue to its backlog card, so `devStartedAt` now rides the backlog twin too (regression-tested).
