blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

Wait, one subtle thing in the issue history: `nextHistory(prevCard, pix.issueState[it.number], bucket, now, hasPrev)` — for the issue cards, `hasPrev` is the global snapshot hasPrev. Note `prevIndex` resolves `ix.issue[issue]` to backlog card preferentially (backlog wins over development card). And `issueState` records which bucket. OK.

Another check on the history dedupe for issue cards: `if (prevKey !== key) h.push(...)` — this one has the dedupe naturally (only pushes on change). Only the terminalAt path lacks the guard.

Edge: for issues, when a card disappears (issue closed or ai_developed), its history is dropped (no carry). Fine.

31:function resolveMachineAuthor(jobParams, config) {
88:    resolveMachineAuthor: resolveMachineAuthor,
/**
 * Machine-author resolution for the #687 PR lifecycle.
 *
 * Whose login counts as "the machine" (the bot the harness authors PRs
 * through) is deployment-specific — this repo never hardcodes it. All
 * machine-keyed guards (the `notMachine` review rule, the rework re-arm
 * in PR-anchored reviews, the SM `prMachineAuthor` query gate) resolve through
 * this single helper. Resolution order:
 *
 *   1. `jobParams.machineAuthor` — the JSON parameter at factory setup:
 *      factory-sm.yml `machine-author` input lands in the `dmtools run`
 *      override (`{"params":{"jobParams":{...,"machineAuthor":"..."}}}}`).
 *      The global-level knob: set once by the harness (machine-sm.yml),
 *      valid for every repo the factory runs against.
 *   2. `config.machineAuthor` — the per-repo `.dmtools/config.js` knob,
 *      for fleets where different repos run different bots.
 *   3. `null` — no machine author configured. Every guard keyed on it is
 *      inert/fail-closed per guard: all green PRs are reviewable
 *      (notMachine inert), no `agent:rework` re-arm on verdicts, and the
 *      SM `prMachineAuthor` rules match nothing (no auto legs at all).
 *      Note: `pr_approved` arming on APPROVE is NOT author-gated — the
 *      owner rule auto-approves external PRs too; only auto-REWORK is
 *      machine-only.
 *
 * @param {Object|null} jobParams job params carrying an optional override
 *                                (accepts the sm ctx: it exposes the same
 *                                `machineAuthor` field).
 * @param {Object|null} config    project config (.dmtools/config.js)
 * @returns {string|null} the machine login, or null when unconfigured
 */
function resolveMachineAuthor(jobParams, config) {
    if (jobParams && jobParams.machineAuthor) {
        return String(jobParams.machineAuthor);
    }
    if (config && config.machineAuthor) {
        return String(config.machineAuthor);
    }
    return null;
}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT (re-verified on head c14d241 — still unfixed): `?fixture=` fetches an arbitrary URL, and snapshot hrefs are not scheme-checked — together they make the board injectable**

Two related gaps in the new v3 surfaces, both unchanged:

1. `FIXTURE` comes straight from the query string and is passed to `fetch` unvalidated. Anyone can craft `index.html?fixture=https://attacker.example/payload.json` and render fully attacker-controlled board content (fake PRs, titles, statuses) under this site's origin — a credible spoofing vector for a public board, since the page never indicates the data didn't come from a `factory-data` snapshot.

2. Card/pill hrefs use snapshot fields verbatim (only HTML-escaped):

```js
var href = isIssue ? (c.url || CFG.prUrl(c.repo, num, 'issues')) : CFG.prUrl(c.repo, num);
```

`esc()` escapes quotes/angle brackets but **not** URL schemes, so a `"url": "javascript:…"` value in a snapshot (or in a fixture JSON) survives into `href` and executes on click. The live data source is the machine's own factory-data branch (trusted), which is why this is IMPORTANT rather than BLOCKING — but the `?fixture=` param hands the untrusted case to anyone who can paste a link.

**Suggested hardening (a few lines total):**
- Restrict the fixture to same-origin/relative paths: `if (FIXTURE && /^(https?:)?\/\//.test(FIXTURE) && FIXTURE.indexOf(location.origin) !== 0) FIXTURE = null;` — the visual-check usage (`?fixture=visual-check/fixture.json`) is relative and keeps working.
- Allowlist the scheme when building hrefs: `function safeHref(u) { return /^https?:\/\//i.test(u) ? u : ''; }` and fall back to `CFG.prUrl(...)` when the snapshot URL fails the check (also covers `c.repo` shape).

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION (re-verified — still unfixed): progress-bar aria-label is vacuous**

```js
return '<div class="lane-bar" role="img" aria-label="' + s.total + ' of ' +
  s.total + '">' + ...
```

This always renders `"N of N"` — the one quantity that carries no information (the same number twice). For a `role="img"` element the label is what a screen reader gets instead of the bar; make it state the actual progress, e.g.:

```js
'aria-label="' + s.total + ' items: ' + s.done + ' done, ' +
  s.inflight + ' in flight, ' + s.queued + ' queued' +
  (s.blocked ? ', ' + s.blocked + ' blocked' : '') + '"'
```

Trivial change, matches the "readable at a glance" goal of the ticket (readable by everyone, including AT users).

- **PR #**: 675

- **Title**: gh-672 Factory Board v3 — readable progress, details drawer (state history + timings), issue backlog lanes, token spend
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-672` → `main`
- **State**: open

- **Deletions**: -74
- **Created**: 2026-10-03T20:05:50Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-03T21:09:39Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Factory Board v3 (`site/factory/`) + additive snapshot schema v3 (`js/factoryState.js`, `js/smAgent.js`): readable per-lane progress, a click-to-open details drawer, issue backlog lanes, and optional per-leg token spend — all fed by the same SM tick snapshots, no new scrapers.

### Key decisions
- **Schema stays 2, all additions optional**: per-card `history` (state timeline, accumulated tick-over-tick like the v2 timestamps, capped at 24), top-level `backlog` (buckets: `blocked` label > assigned to `machineAuthor` > `agent:dev` > inbox), optional per-card `tokens` (leg/at/prompt/completion/total). Old snapshots keep rendering; the drawer derives a timeline from v2 timestamp fields when `history` is absent and renders `tokens — not reported by this factory` as fallback.
- **Token source is a contract, not a scraper**: factories whose legs report usage (fa's bench) drop a keyed JSON file (`statePublish.tokensFile`, default `outputs/token_usage/factory_tokens.json`); `readTokensFile()` degrades to null on any miss — never fails the tick.
- **One search call per tick** now fetches ALL open issues (`repo:X is:issue is:open`), feeding both the development lane and the backlog; dev-lane and backlog twins of an issue share one history array.
- **Board**: cards keep their GitHub href (middle-click/new tab) but a plain click opens the inline drawer (state history newest-first, `2h13m`-style per-state timings with proportional bars, token table with per-card total; esc/backdrop/✕ close). Backlog renders as four columns under the pipeline, blocked visually distinct. `?fixture=` + bundled `visual-check/fixture.json` pin "now" for deterministic captures; `?drawer=pr-817@validating` deep-links.
- Fixed a latent carry bug en route: `prevIndex` resolves an issue to its backlog card, so `devStartedAt` now rides the backlog twin too (regression-tested).
- Added `.dmtools/credential-helper.log` to `.gitignore` (local credential log — a previous run accidentally committed it).

### How to verify
```bash
FILES=$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js $FILES   # 1272 pass; the 45 failures are the known harness mock gaps (baseline 1251/45 — same set)
bash site/factory/visual-check/capture.sh      # regenerates the 5 fixture PNGs (needs headless chromium)
# or open: site/factory/index.html?fixture=visual-check/fixture.json&drawer=pr-817@validating
```
`js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` grew 29→50 tests (history accumulation, backlog bucketing, tokens normalization, tokens-file contract, devStartedAt carry). Visual-check fixtures regenerated for the new surfaces at all four viewports plus a drawer-open frame; pages deploy stays green (fixtures are excluded from `_site`).

## Description

# Factory Board v3 — readable progress, details drawer, backlog lanes, token spend

Owner-directed (2026-10-03). The board at `site/factory/` (zero-build, state snapshots from `factory-data` branches) needs four upgrades. All data must keep coming from the SM tick snapshots — no new scrapers.

## 1. Progress line is unreadable

Dots now encode per-PR status, but it's impossible to answer "how much is left" at a glance. Replace/augment the dot row per lane with a compact summary: `N total · M done · K in-flight · Q queued` (+ blocked count where relevant) and a thin progress bar per lane. Dots may stay as decoration, the numbers must be readable.

## 2. Click → details drawer → PR

Clicking a PR (dot, card, or row) opens a details drawer (inline panel, no page nav):
- header: PR number, title, head sha, current state + labels, **link to the PR** (opens github.com in a new tab)
- body: **full state history** — the sequence of states this PR went through with timestamps (from the snapshot history), newest first
- **timings** — how long the PR sat in each state (`validating 42m`, `approved→validated 5m`, `parked 2h13m`), so bottlenecks are analyzable later. Raw durations + a simple bar per state.

## 3. Issues as backlog lanes

The board shows PRs only; issues are invisible. Add a backlog section fed by the same snapshots (extend the SM tick snapshot with open issues: number, title, assignee, labels):
- columns by state: **assigned to ai-teammate (in dev)** · **agent:dev queued** · **blocked** (the `blocked` label = owner hold, must be its own column and visually distinct) · inbox (no label/assignee)
- each issue clickable → same details drawer (issue states: assigned → dev → PR opened → …), link to the issue.

## 4. Token spend per action (details)

fa legs already report token usage (bench); more factories will follow. Extend the snapshot with per-leg token counters (prompt/completion/total per run where available) and show them in the details drawer: per-action table (leg, when, tokens) + a per-PR total. Graceful "—" when a factory doesn't report tokens yet — schema stays optional.

## Acceptance

- Board still zero-build, still reads `factory-data` snapshots (schema addition = additive, old snapshots keep rendering).
- Lane summaries readable at a glance; details drawer works for PRs and issues; timings render; token table renders with fallback.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #675._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/factoryState.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-03):
🚨 **BLOCKING: merged cards' state history destroys itself within ~4h of the merge**

`nextHistory`'s `terminalAt` path appends unconditionally, but merged cards are **rebuilt every tick** while they sit in the 24h `merged_recent` window (`buildFactoryState` re-derives the card from `prevCard` each tick, `js/factoryState.js:493`). So every tick appends *another* `{merged_recent, at: mergedAt}` entry:

```js
if (terminalAt) {
    h.push({ state: key, at: terminalAt });   // no dedupe — pushes every tick
    return capHistory(h);
}
```

Reproduced by chaining `buildFactoryState` over 31 ticks (10-min cadence):

```
tick 1 history: [pr_created, validating, merged_recent@09:30]   ← correct
after 31 ticks: 24 × {merged_recent, at 09:30}                  ← real history fully evicted
```

After `HISTORY_CAP` (24) ticks (~4h at the standard 10-min cadence) the card's entire real pipeline timeline (`pr_created → review → approved_queue → validating`) is sliced out of the snapshot. The drawer then renders 24 identical "Merged" rows with `0m` durations — the ticket's headline deliverable (per-state timings for bottleneck analysis) is gone exactly for the cards where it matters most. The new test only covers the *first* merge transition, so it can't see this.

**Fix** (one guard — skip the append when the carried history already ends in that state):

```js
if (terminalAt) {
    if (!h.length || h[h.length - 1].state !== key) {
        h.push({ state: key, at: terminalAt });
    }
    return capHistory(h);
}
```

and add a regression test that builds the merged state tick-over-tick and asserts the history length stays at 3 with no duplicate terminal entries.

---

### Thread 2 — `.dmtools/credential-helper.log`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-03):
🚨 **BLOCKING: this PR commits the credential-helper log it claims to gitignore**

The diff **adds** `.dmtools/credential-helper.log` as a new tracked file (4 lines of `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN credential served …` trace events) *and* adds the path to `.gitignore`. Those two changes contradict each other: `.gitignore` has **no effect on tracked files**, so the local run artifact is now permanently in the repo and every future run appends more lines that will show up in diffs (this very branch already went through an unresolved both-added merge conflict over this file).

Context per `AGENTS.md`: this is a **public, product-agnostic** repo and local dmtools run artifacts must never be committed. The log content contains no secret values (env var *name* + timestamps only), but committing credential-serving traces is exactly the artifact class that must stay out; the PR description itself says the goal was to stop tracking "a previous run accidentally committed it" — the change does the opposite.

**Fix:**

```bash
git rm --cached .dmtools/credential-helper.log
```

Keep the `.gitignore` line (correct), drop the file from the commit. Please also verify no earlier commit on this branch left the file in history (`git log --all --oneline -- .dmtools/credential-helper.log`) — a history that ever contained it cannot be cleaned by `.gitignore` alone.

---

### Thread 3 — `site/factory/app.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-03):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: development-lane issue cards never open the details drawer**

The render pass indexes only PR cards from the pipeline lanes:

```js
list.forEach(function (c) {
    if (c && c.pr != null) boardIndex['pr-' + c.pr + '@' + l.id] =
      { item: c, repo: st_repo, laneId: l.id };
});
```

A card in the **development lane** is an issue card, so it gets `data-key="issue-402@development"` — a key that is never added to `boardIndex` (only the backlog columns are indexed below). `onCardClick` → `drawerCtxFor` returns `null` → `preventDefault` is skipped → the click falls through and **navigates to GitHub** instead of opening the drawer. Meanwhile the same issue's backlog twin (`issue-402@in_dev`) opens the drawer fine. Two twins, two different behaviors — and the "In dev" card, the one an operator watches most, is the one that silently loses the feature.

Ticket AC says "details drawer works for PRs and issues"; for in-dev issues it only half-works.

**Fix:** index issue cards in the lanes loop too (`boardIndex['issue-' + c.issue + '@' + l.id] = …`), or resolve `issue-N@development` to the backlog twin's context in `drawerCtxFor`.

---

### Thread 4 — `site/factory/app.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-03):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `?fixture=` fetches an arbitrary URL, and snapshot hrefs are not scheme-checked — together they make the board injectable**

Two related gaps in the new v3 surfaces:

1. `FIXTURE` comes straight from the query string and is passed to `fetch` unvalidated. Anyone can craft
   `index.html?fixture=https://attacker.example/payload.json` and render fully attacker-controlled board content (fake PRs, titles, statuses) under this site's origin — a credible spoofing vector for a public board, since the page never indicates the data didn't come from a `factory-data` snapshot.

2. Card/pill hrefs use snapshot fields verbatim (only HTML-escaped):
   ```js
   var href = isIssue ? (c.url || CFG.prUrl(c.repo, num, 'issues')) : CFG.prUrl(c.repo, num);
   ```
   `esc()` escapes quotes/angle brackets but **not** URL schemes, so a `"url": "javascript:…"` value in a snapshot (or in a fixture JSON) survives into `href` and executes on click. The live data source is the machine's own factory-data branch (trusted), which is why this is IMPORTANT rather than BLOCKING — but the `?fixture=` param hands the untrusted case to anyone who can paste a link.

**Suggested hardening (a few lines total):**
- Restrict the fixture to same-origin/relative paths: `if (FIXTURE && /^(https?:)?\/\//.test(FIXTURE) && FIXTURE.indexOf(location.origin) !== 0) FIXTURE = null;` — the visual-check usage (`?fixture=visual-check/fixture.json`) is relative and keeps working.
- Allowlist the scheme when building hrefs: `function safeHref(u) { return /^https?:\/\//i.test(u) ? u : ''; }` and fall back to `CFG.prUrl(...)` when the snapshot URL fails the check (also covers `c.repo` shape).

---

### Thread 5 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-03):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the backlog silently truncates at the search API's first page and is unbounded**

The v3 query fetches ALL open issues (`repo:X is:issue is:open`) in one call. GitHub search returns at most one page per call (30 by default, 100 with `per_page`), and `github_search_issues` here passes no paging — so on a repo with more open issues than one page, the `inbox` bucket (everything unassigned/unlabeled) is **silently truncated** while `backlogCounts` presents the partial view as authoritative ("N total"). Snapshots also grow without a bound as the issue count grows — they're re-published to the data branch every 10 minutes and rendered in full.

Practical impact today is low (the active repos have modest open-issue counts), but the snapshot's contract should be honest about completeness. Options:

- pass an explicit `perPage`/sort (e.g. `sort:created&order:desc`, newest N) and document the cap next to `backlogCounts`;
- or cap the inbox bucket in `buildFactoryState` (e.g. 50 newest) so the JSON size stays bounded regardless of repo;
- at minimum, note the page limit in the README's backlog section so a truncated lane isn't mistaken for "empty".

The change from the label-filtered query to all-issues is also a behavior change worth a line in the PR description's verify notes: on busy repos the search now matches far more items per tick (cost is fine — still one call — but the payload is not).

---

### Thread 6 — `site/factory/app.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-03):
💡 **SUGGESTION: progress-bar aria-label is vacuous**

```js
return '<div class="lane-bar" role="img" aria-label="' + s.total + ' of ' +
  s.total + '">' + ...
```

This always renders `"N of N"` — the one quantity that carries no information (it's the same number twice). For a `role="img"` element the label is what a screen reader gets instead of the ba…

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

31:function resolveMachineAuthor(jobParams, config) {
88:    resolveMachineAuthor: resolveMachineAuthor,
/**
 * Machine-author resolution for the #687 PR lifecycle.
 *
 * Whose login counts as "the machine" (the bot the harness authors PRs
 * through) is deployment-specific — this repo never hardcodes it. All
 * machine-keyed guards (the `notMachine` review rule, the rework re-arm
 * in PR-anchored reviews, the SM `prMachineAuthor` query gate) resolve through
 * this single helper. Resolution order:
 *
 *   1. `jobParams.machineAuthor` — the JSON parameter at factory setup:
 *      factory-sm.yml `machine-author` input lands in the `dmtools run`
 *      override (`{"params":{"jobParams":{...,"machineAuthor":"..."}}}}`).
 *      The global-level knob: set once by the harness (machine-sm.yml),
 *      valid for every repo the factory runs against.
 *   2. `config.machineAuthor` — the per-repo `.dmtools/config.js` knob,
 *      for fleets where different repos run different bots.
 *   3. `null` — no machine author configured. Every guard keyed on it is
 *      inert/fail-closed per guard: all green PRs are reviewable
 *      (notMachine inert), no `agent:rework` re-arm on verdicts, and the
 *      SM `prMachineAuthor` rules match nothing (no auto legs at all).
 *      Note: `pr_approved` arming on APPROVE is NOT author-gated — the
 *      owner rule auto-approves external PRs too; only auto-REWORK is
 *      machine-only.
 *
 * @param {Object|null} jobParams job params carrying an optional override
 *                                (accepts the sm ctx: it exposes the same
 *                                `machineAuthor` field).
 * @param {Object|null} config    project config (.dmtools/config.js)
 * @returns {string|null} the machine login, or null when unconfigured
 */
function resolveMachineAuthor(jobParams, config) {
    if (jobParams && jobParams.machineAuthor) {
        return String(jobParams.machineAuthor);
    }
    if (config && config.machineAuthor) {
        return String(config.machineAuthor);
    }
    return null;
}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT (re-verified on head c14d241 — still unfixed): `?fixture=` fetches an arbitrary URL, and snapshot hrefs are not scheme-checked — together they make the board injectable**

Two related gaps in the new v3 surfaces, both unchanged:

1. `FIXTURE` comes straight from the query string and is passed to `fetch` unvalidated. Anyone can craft `index.html?fixture=https://attacker.example/payload.json` and render fully attacker-controlled board content (fake PRs, titles, statuses) under this site's origin — a credible spoofing vector for a public board, since the page never indicates the data didn't come from a `factory-data` snapshot.

2. Card/pill hrefs use snapshot fields verbatim (only HTML-escaped):

```js
var href = isIssue ? (c.url || CFG.prUrl(c.repo, num, 'issues')) : CFG.prUrl(c.repo, num);
```

`esc()` escapes quotes/angle brackets but **not** URL schemes, so a `"url": "javascript:…"` value in a snapshot (or in a fixture JSON) survives into `href` and executes on click. The live data source is the machine's own factory-data branch (trusted), which is why this is IMPORTANT rather than BLOCKING — but the `?fixture=` param hands the untrusted case to anyone who can paste a link.

**Suggested hardening (a few lines total):**
- Restrict the fixture to same-origin/relative paths: `if (FIXTURE && /^(https?:)?\/\//.test(FIXTURE) && FIXTURE.indexOf(location.origin) !== 0) FIXTURE = null;` — the visual-check usage (`?fixture=visual-check/fixture.json`) is relative and keeps working.
- Allowlist the scheme when building hrefs: `function safeHref(u) { return /^https?:\/\//i.test(u) ? u : ''; }` and fall back to `CFG.prUrl(...)` when the snapshot URL fails the check (also covers `c.repo` shape).

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 675
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/675
- **Title**: gh-672 Factory Board v3 — readable progress, details drawer (state history + timings), issue backlog lanes, token spend
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-672` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1449
- **Deletions**: -74
- **Created**: 2026-10-03T20:05:50Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-03T21:09:39Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Factory Board v3 (`site/factory/`) + additive snapshot schema v3 (`js/factoryState.js`, `js/smAgent.js`): readable per-lane progress, a click-to-open details drawer, issue backlog lanes, and optional per-leg token spend — all fed by the same SM tick snapshots, no new scrapers.

### Key decisions
- **Schema stays 2, all additions optional**: per-card `history` (state timeline, accumulated tick-over-tick like the v2 timestamps, capped at 24), top-level `backlog` (buckets: `blocked` label > assigned to `machineAuthor` > `agent:dev` > inbox), optional per-card `tokens` (leg/at/prompt/completion/total). Old snapshots keep rendering; the drawer derives a timeline from v2 timestamp fields when `history` is absent and renders `tokens — not reported by this factory` as fallback.
- **Token source is a contract, not a scraper**: factories whose legs report usage (fa's bench) drop a keyed JSON file (`statePublish.tokensFile`, default `outputs/token_usage/factory_tokens.json`); `readTokensFile()` degrades to null on any miss — never fails the tick.
- **One search call per tick** now fetches ALL open issues (`repo:X is:issue is:open`), feeding both the development lane and the backlog; dev-lane and backlog twins of an issue share one history array.
- **Board**: cards keep their GitHub href (middle-click/new tab) but a plain click opens the inline drawer (state history newest-first, `2h13m`-style per-state timings with proportional bars, token table with per-card total; esc/backdrop/✕ close). Backlog renders as four columns under the pipeline, blocked visually distinct. `?fixture=` + bundled `visual-check/fixture.json` pin "now" for deterministic captures; `?drawer=pr-817@validating` deep-links.
- Fixed a latent carry bug en route: `prevIndex` resolves an issue to its backlog card, so `devStartedAt` now rides the backlog twin too (regression-tested).
- Added `.dmtools/credential-helper.log` to `.gitignore` (local credential log — a previous run accidentally committed it).

### How to verify
```bash
FILES=$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js $FILES   # 1272 pass; the 45 failures are the known harness mock gaps (baseline 1251/45 — same set)
bash site/factory/visual-check/capture.sh      # regenerates the 5 fixture PNGs (needs headless chromium)
# or open: site/factory/index.html?fixture=visual-check/fixture.json&drawer=pr-817@validating
```
`js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` grew 29→50 tests (history accumulation, backlog bucketing, tokens normalization, tokens-file contract, devStartedAt carry). Visual-check fixtures regenerated for the new surfaces at all four viewports plus a drawer-open frame; pages deploy stays green (fixtures are excluded from `_site`).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SM[SM tick] -->|"gh search: all open issues"| FS[buildFactoryState]
  SM -->|optional tokens file| FS
  FS -->|"lanes + history + backlog + tokens (schema 2, additive)"| PUB[publish → factory-data branch]
  PUB --> BOARD[site/factory board]
  BOARD --> SUM[lane summaries + progress bars]
  BOARD --> BL[backlog: in_dev · queued · blocked · inbox]
  BOARD --> DR[details drawer: history + timings + tokens]
```

</details>

## Description

# Factory Board v3 — readable progress, details drawer, backlog lanes, token spend

Owner-directed (2026-10-03). The board at `site/factory/` (zero-build, state snapshots from `factory-data` branches) needs four upgrades. All data must keep coming from the SM tick snapshots — no new scrapers.

## 1. Progress line is unreadable

Dots now encode per-PR status, but it's impossible to answer "how much is left" at a glance. Replace/augment the dot row per lane with a compact summary: `N total · M done · K in-flight · Q queued` (+ blocked count where relevant) and a thin progress bar per lane. Dots may stay as decoration, the numbers must be readable.

## 2. Click → details drawer → PR

Clicking a PR (dot, card, or row) opens a details drawer (inline panel, no page nav):
- header: PR number, title, head sha, current state + labels, **link to the PR** (opens github.com in a new tab)
- body: **full state history** — the sequence of states this PR went through with timestamps (from the snapshot history), newest first
- **timings** — how long the PR sat in each state (`validating 42m`, `approved→validated 5m`, `parked 2h13m`), so bottlenecks are analyzable later. Raw durations + a simple bar per state.

## 3. Issues as backlog lanes

The board shows PRs only; issues are invisible. Add a backlog section fed by the same snapshots (extend the SM tick snapshot with open issues: number, title, assignee, labels):
- columns by state: **assigned to ai-teammate (in dev)** · **agent:dev queued** · **blocked** (the `blocked` label = owner hold, must be its own column and visually distinct) · inbox (no label/assignee)
- each issue clickable → same details drawer (issue states: assigned → dev → PR opened → …), link to the issue.

## 4. Token spend per action (details)

fa legs already report token usage (bench); more factories will follow. Extend the snapshot with per-leg token counters (prompt/completion/total per run where available) and show them in the details drawer: per-action table (leg, when, tokens) + a per-PR total. Graceful "—" when a factory doesn't report tokens yet — schema stays optional.

## Acceptance

- Board still zero-build, still reads `factory-data` snapshots (schema addition = additive, old snapshots keep rendering).
- Lane summaries readable at a glance; details drawer works for PRs and issues; timings render; token table renders with fallback.
- `visual-check` fixtures updated for the new surfaces (see `site/factory/visual-check/`).

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #675._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/factoryState.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-03):
🚨 **BLOCKING: merged cards' state history destroys itself within ~4h of the merge**

`nextHistory`'s `terminalAt` path appends unconditionally, but merged cards are **rebuilt every tick** while they sit in the 24h `merged_recent` window (`buildFactoryState` re-derives the card from `prevCard` each tick, `js/factoryState.js:493`). So every tick appends *another* `{merged_recent, at: mergedAt}` entry:

```js
if (terminalAt) {
    h.push({ state: key, at: terminalAt });   // no dedupe — pushes every tick
    return capHistory(h);
}
```

Reproduced by chaining `buildFactoryState` over 31 ticks (10-min cadence):

```
tick 1 history: [pr_created, validating, merged_recent@09:30]   ← correct
after 31 ticks: 24 × {merged_recent, at 09:30}                  ← real history fully evicted
```

After `HISTORY_CAP` (24) ticks (~4h at the standard 10-min cadence) the card's entire real pipeline timeline (`pr_created → review → approved_queue → validating`) is sliced out of the snapshot. The drawer then renders 24 identical "Merged" rows with `0m` durations — the ticket's headline deliverable (per-state timings for bottleneck analysis) is gone exactly for the cards where it matters most. The new test only covers the *first* merge transition, so it can't see this.

**Fix** (one guard — skip the append when the carried history already ends in that state):

```js
if (terminalAt) {
    if (!h.length || h[h.length - 1].state !== key) {
        h.push({ state: key, at: terminalAt });
    }
    return capHistory(h);
}
```

and add a regression test that builds the merged state tick-over-tick and asserts the history length stays at 3 with no duplicate terminal entries.

---

### Thread 2 — `.dmtools/credential-helper.log`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-03):
🚨 **BLOCKING: this PR commits the credential-helper log it claims to gitignore**

The diff **adds** `.dmtools/credential-helper.log` as a new tracked file (4 lines of `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN credential served …` trace events) *and* adds the path to `.gitignore`. Those two changes contradict each other: `.gitignore` has **no effect on tracked files**, so the local run artifact is now permanently in the repo and every future run appends more lines that will show up in diffs (this very branch already went through an unresolved both-added merge conflict over this file).

Context per `AGENTS.md`: this is a **public, product-agnostic** repo and local dmtools run artifacts must never be committed. The log content contains no secret values (env var *name* + timestamps only), but committing credential-serving traces is exactly the artifact class that must stay out; the PR description itself says the goal was to stop tracking "a previous run accidentally committed it" — the change does the opposite.

**Fix:**

```bash
git rm --cached .dmtools/credential-helper.log
```

Keep the `.gitignore` line (correct), drop the file from the commit. Please also verify no earlier commit on this branch left the file in history (`git log --all --oneline -- .dmtools/credential-helper.log`) — a history that ever contained it cannot be cleaned by `.gitignore` alone.

---

### Thread 3 — `site/factory/app.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-03):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: development-lane issue cards never open the details drawer**

The render pass indexes only PR cards from the pipeline lanes:

```js
list.forEach(function (c) {
    if (c && c.pr != null) boardIndex['pr-' + c.pr + '@' + l.id] =
      { item: c, repo: st_repo, laneId: l.id };
});
```

A card in the **development lane** is an issue card, so it gets `data-key="issue-402@development"` — a key that is never added to `boardIndex` (only the backlog columns are indexed below). `onCardClick` → `drawerCtxFor` returns `null` → `preventDefault` is skipped → the click falls through and **navigates to GitHub** instead of opening the drawer. Meanwhile the same issue's backlog twin (`issue-402@in_dev`) opens the drawer fine. Two twins, two different behaviors — and the "In dev" card, the one an operator watches most, is the one that silently loses the feature.

Ticket AC says "details drawer works for PRs and issues"; for in-dev issues it only half-works.

**Fix:** index issue cards in the lanes loop too (`boardIndex['issue-' + c.issue + '@' + l.id] = …`), or resolve `issue-N@development` to the backlog twin's context in `drawerCtxFor`.

---

### Thread 4 — `site/factory/app.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-03):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `?fixture=` fetches an arbitrary URL, and snapshot hrefs are not scheme-checked — together they make the board injectable**

Two related gaps in the new v3 surfaces:

1. `FIXTURE` comes straight from the query string and is passed to `fetch` unvalidated. Anyone can craft
   `index.html?fixture=https://attacker.example/payload.json` and render fully attacker-controlled board content (fake PRs, titles, statuses) under this site's origin — a credible spoofing vector for a public board, since the page never indicates the data didn't come from a `factory-data` snapshot.

2. Card/pill hrefs use snapshot fields verbatim (only HTML-escaped):
   ```js
   var href = isIssue ? (c.url || CFG.prUrl(c.repo, num, 'issues')) : CFG.prUrl(c.repo, num);
   ```
   `esc()` escapes quotes/angle brackets but **not** URL schemes, so a `"url": "javascript:…"` value in a snapshot (or in a fixture JSON) survives into `href` and executes on click. The live data source is the machine's own factory-data branch (trusted), which is why this is IMPORTANT rather than BLOCKING — but the `?fixture=` param hands the untrusted case to anyone who can paste a link.

**Suggested hardening (a few lines total):**
- Restrict the fixture to same-origin/relative paths: `if (FIXTURE && /^(https?:)?\/\//.test(FIXTURE) && FIXTURE.indexOf(location.origin) !== 0) FIXTURE = null;` — the visual-check usage (`?fixture=visual-check/fixture.json`) is relative and keeps working.
- Allowlist the scheme when building hrefs: `function safeHref(u) { return /^https?:\/\//i.test(u) ? u : ''; }` and fall back to `CFG.prUrl(...)` when the snapshot URL fails the check (also covers `c.repo` shape).

---

### Thread 5 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-03):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the backlog silently truncates at the search API's first page and is unbounded**

The v3 query fetches ALL open issues (`repo:X is:issue is:open`) in one call. GitHub search returns at most one page per call (30 by default, 100 with `per_page`), and `github_search_issues` here passes no paging — so on a repo with more open issues than one page, the `inbox` bucket (everything unassigned/unlabeled) is **silently truncated** while `backlogCounts` presents the partial view as authoritative ("N total"). Snapshots also grow without a bound as the issue count grows — they're re-published to the data branch every 10 minutes and rendered in full.

Practical impact today is low (the active repos have modest open-issue counts), but the snapshot's contract should be honest about completeness. Options:

- pass an explicit `perPage`/sort (e.g. `sort:created&order:desc`, newest N) and document the cap next to `backlogCounts`;
- or cap the inbox bucket in `buildFactoryState` (e.g. 50 newest) so the JSON size stays bounded regardless of repo;
- at minimum, note the page limit in the README's backlog section so a truncated lane isn't mistaken for "empty".

The change from the label-filtered query to all-issues is also a behavior change worth a line in the PR description's verify notes: on busy repos the search now matches far more items per tick (cost is fine — still one call — but the payload is not).

      "body": "🚨 **BLOCKING: merged cards' state history destroys itself within ~4h of the merge**

`nextHistory`'s `terminalAt` path appends unconditionally, but merged cards are **rebuilt every tick** while they sit in the 24h `merged_recent` window (`buildFactoryState` re-derives the card from `prevCard` each tick, `js/factoryState.js:493`). So every tick appends *another* `{merged_recent, at: mergedAt}` entry:

```js
if (terminalAt) {
    h.push({ state: key, at: terminalAt });   // no dedupe — pushes every tick
    return capHistory(h);
}
```

Reproduced by chaining `buildFactoryState` over 31 ticks (10-min cadence):

```
tick 1 history: [pr_created, validating, merged_recent@09:30]   ← correct
after 31 ticks: 24 × {merged_recent, at 09:30}                  ← real history fully evicted
```

After `HISTORY_CAP` (24) ticks (~4h at the standard 10-min cadence) the card's entire real pipeline timeline (`pr_created → review → approved_queue → validating`) is sliced out of the snapshot. The drawer then renders 24 identical "Merged" rows with `0m` durations — the ticket's headline deliverable (per-state timings for bottleneck analysis) is gone exactly for the cards where it matters most. The new test only covers the *first* merge transition, so it can't see this.

**Fix** (one guard — skip the append when the carried history already ends in that state):

```js
if (terminalAt) {
    if (!h.length || h[h.length - 1].state !== key) {
        h.push({ state: key, at: terminalAt });
    }
    return capHistory(h);
}
```

and add a regression test that builds the merged state tick-over-tick and asserts the history length stays at 3 with no duplicate terminal entries."

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `instruction…

31:function resolveMachineAuthor(jobParams, config) {
88:    resolveMachineAuthor: resolveMachineAuthor,
/**
 * Machine-author resolution for the #687 PR lifecycle.
 *
 * Whose login counts as "the machine" (the bot the harness authors PRs
 * through) is deployment-specific — this repo never hardcodes it. All
 * machine-keyed guards (the `notMachine` review rule, the rework re-arm
 * in PR-anchored reviews, the SM `prMachineAuthor` query gate) resolve through
 * this single helper. Resolution order:
 *
 *   1. `jobParams.machineAuthor` — the JSON parameter at factory setup:
 *      factory-sm.yml `machine-author` input lands in the `dmtools run`
 *      override (`{"params":{"jobParams":{...,"machineAuthor":"..."}}}}`).
 *      The global-level knob: set once by the harness (machine-sm.yml),
 *      valid for every repo the factory runs against.
 *   2. `config.machineAuthor` — the per-repo `.dmtools/config.js` knob,
 *      for fleets where different repos run different bots.
 *   3. `null` — no machine author configured. Every guard keyed on it is
 *      inert/fail-closed per guard: all green PRs are reviewable
 *      (notMachine inert), no `agent:rework` re-arm on verdicts, and the
 *      SM `prMachineAuthor` rules match nothing (no auto legs at all).
 *      Note: `pr_approved` arming on APPROVE is NOT author-gated — the
 *      owner rule auto-approves external PRs too; only auto-REWORK is
 *      machine-only.
 *
 * @param {Object|null} jobParams job params carrying an optional override
 *                                (accepts the sm ctx: it exposes the same
 *                                `machineAuthor` field).
 * @param {Object|null} config    project config (.dmtools/config.js)
 * @returns {string|null} the machine login, or null when unconfigured
 */
function resolveMachineAuthor(jobParams, config) {
    if (jobParams && jobParams.machineAuthor) {
        return String(jobParams.machineAuthor);
    }
    if (config && config.machineAuthor) {
        return String(config.machineAuthor);
    }
    return null;
}

+

+### `card.history` — state timeline (details drawer + timings)
+
+Every card may carry `history: [{state, at}]` (oldest first), accumulated

+```

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT (re-verified on head c14d241 — still unfixed): `?fixture=` fetches an arbitrary URL, and snapshot hrefs are not scheme-checked — together they make the board injectable**

Two related gaps in the new v3 surfaces, both unchanged:

1. `FIXTURE` comes straight from the query string and is passed to `fetch` unvalidated. Anyone can craft `index.html?fixture=https://attacker.example/payload.json` and render fully attacker-controlled board content (fake PRs, titles, statuses) under this site's origin — a credible spoofing vector for a public board, since the page never indicates the data didn't come from a `factory-data` snapshot.

2. Card/pill hrefs use snapshot fields verbatim (only HTML-escaped):

```js
var href = isIssue ? (c.url || CFG.prUrl(c.repo, num, 'issues')) : CFG.prUrl(c.repo, num);
```

`esc()` escapes quotes/angle brackets but **not** URL schemes, so a `"url": "javascript:…"` value in a snapshot (or in a fixture JSON) survives into `href` and executes on click. The live data source is the machine's own factory-data branch (trusted), which is why this is IMPORTANT rather than BLOCKING — but the `?fixture=` param hands the untrusted case to anyone who can paste a link.

**Suggested hardening (a few lines total):**
- Restrict the fixture to same-origin/relative paths: `if (FIXTURE && /^(https?:)?\/\//.test(FIXTURE) && FIXTURE.indexOf(location.origin) !== 0) FIXTURE = null;` — the visual-check usage (`?fixture=visual-check/fixture.json`) is relative and keeps working.
- Allowlist the scheme when building hrefs: `function safeHref(u) { return /^https?:\/\//i.test(u) ? u : ''; }` and fall back to `CFG.prUrl(...)` when the snapshot URL fails the check (also covers `c.repo` shape).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 675
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/675
- **Title**: gh-672 Factory Board v3 — readable progress, details drawer (state history + timings), issue backlog lanes, token spend
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-672` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1449
- **Deletions**: -74
- **Created**: 2026-10-03T20:05:50Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-03T21:09:39Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Factory Board v3 (`site/factory/`) + additive snapshot schema v3 (`js/factoryState.js`, `js/smAgent.js`): readable per-lane progress, a click-to-open details drawer, issue backlog lanes, and optional per-leg token spend — all fed by the same SM tick snapshots, no new scrapers.

### Key decisions
- **Schema stays 2, all additions optional**: per-card `history` (state timeline, accumulated tick-over-tick like the v2 timestamps, capped at 24), top-level `backlog` (buckets: `blocked` label > assigned to `machineAuthor` > `agent:dev` > inbox), optional per-card `tokens` (leg/at/prompt/completion/total). Old snapshots keep rendering; the drawer derives a timeline from v2 timestamp fields when `history` is absent and renders `tokens — not reported by this factory` as fallback.
- **Token source is a contract, not a scraper**: factories whose legs report usage (fa's bench) drop a keyed JSON file (`statePublish.tokensFile`, default `outputs/token_usage/factory_tokens.json`); `readTokensFile()` degrades to null on any miss — never fails the tick.
- **One search call per tick** now fetches ALL open issues (`repo:X is:issue is:open`), feeding both the development lane and the backlog; dev-lane and backlog twins of an issue share one history array.
- **Board**: cards keep their GitHub href (middle-click/new tab) but a plain click opens the inline drawer (state history newest-first, `2h13m`-style per-state timings with proportional bars, token table with per-card total; esc/backdrop/✕ close). Backlog renders as four columns under the pipeline, blocked visually distinct. `?fixture=` + bundled `visual-check/fixture.json` pin "now" for deterministic captures; `?drawer=pr-817@validating` deep-links.
- Fixed a latent carry bug en route: `prevIndex` resolves an issue to its backlog card, so `devStartedAt` now rides the backlog twin too (regression-tested).
- Added `.dmtools/credential-helper.log` to `.gitignore` (local credential log — a previous run accidentally committed it).

### How to verify
```bash
FILES=$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js $FILES   # 1272 pass; the 45 failures are the known harness mock gaps (baseline 1251/45 — same set)
bash site/factory/visual-check/capture.sh      # regenerates the 5 fixture PNGs (needs headless chromium)
# or open: site/factory/index.html?fixture=visual-check/fixture.json&drawer=pr-817@validating
```
`js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js` grew 29→50 tests (history accumulation, backlog bucketing, tokens normalization, tokens-file contract, devStartedAt carry). Visual-check fixtures regenerated for the new surfaces at all four viewports plus a drawer-open frame; pages deploy stays green (fixtures are excluded from `_site`).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SM[SM tick] -->|"gh search: all open issues"| FS[buildFactoryState]
  SM -->|optional tokens file| FS
  FS -->|"lanes + history + backlog + tokens (schema 2, additive)"| PUB[publish → factory-data branch]
  PUB --> BOARD[site/factory board]
  BOARD --> SUM[lane summaries + progress bars]
  BOARD --> BL[backlog: in_dev · queued · blocked · inbox]
  BOARD --> DR[details drawer: history + timings + tokens]
```

</details>

## Description

# Factory Board v3 — readable progress, details drawer, backlog lanes, token spend

Owner-directed (2026-10-03). The board at `site/factory/` (zero-build, state snapshots from `factory-data` branches) needs four upgrades. All data must keep coming from the SM tick snapshots — no new scrapers.

## 1. Progress line is unreadable

Dots now encode per-PR status, but it's impossible to answer "how much is left" at a glance. Replace/augment the dot row per lane with a compact summary: `N total · M done · K in-flight · Q queued` (+ blocked count where relevant) and a thin progress bar per lane. Dots may stay as decoration, the numbers must be readable.

## 2. Click → details drawer → PR

Clicking a PR (dot, card, or row) opens a details drawer (inline panel, no page nav):
- header: PR number, title, head sha, current state + labels, **link to the PR** (opens github.com in a new tab)
- body: **full state history** — the sequence of states this PR went through with timestamps (from the snapshot history), newest first
- **timings** — how long the PR sat in each state (`validating 42m`, `approved→validated 5m`, `parked 2h13m`), so bottlenecks are analyzable later. Raw durations + a simple bar per state.

## 3. Issues as backlog lanes

The board shows PRs only; issues are invisible. Add a backlog section fed by the same snapshots (extend the SM tick snapshot with open issues: number, title, assignee, labels):
- columns by state: **assigned to ai-teammate (in dev)** · **agent:dev queued** · **blocked** (the `blocked` label = owner hold, must be its own column and visually distinct) · inbox (no label/assignee)
- each issue clickable → same details drawer (issue states: assigned → dev → PR opened → …), link to the issue.

## 4. Token spend per action (details)

fa legs already report token usage (bench); more factories will follow. Extend the snapshot with per-leg token counters (prompt/completion/total per run where available) and show them in the details drawer: per-action table (leg, when, tokens) + a per-PR total. Graceful "—" when a factory doesn't report tokens yet — schema stays optional.

## Acceptance

- Board still zero-build, still reads `factory-data` snapshots (schema addition = additive, old snapshots keep rendering).
- Lane summaries readable at a glance; details drawer works for PRs and issues; timings render; token table renders with fallback.
- `visual-check` fixtures updated for the new surfaces (see `site/factory/visual-check/`).
- Pages deploy stays green.
